title: Двойное недоразумение с полицией  (A Double Misunderstanding with the Police)

segments.t: When the police officer calls Nagiyev to verify Chef Barinov's identity, a terrified Nagiyev assumes the police have discovered the kidnapped photographer and immediately denies everything. Seconds later, Vika calls Nagiyev from the hospital after discovering Barinov's empty bed.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'No, that is not me.' Dmitry anchors the line on 'there is no', while 'I' completes the thought.
'You have the wrong person.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'you' and finishing on 'to make a mistake'. Dmitry answers right away.
'That is all. Goodbye.' In Russian, the idea of 'all' flows naturally into 'all' without extra filler words.
'The police! Apparently.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'police' before landing on 'apparently'.
'Why is he taking so long?' The grammar packs 'what' and 'there is no' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Senya answers right away.
'What are we supposed to do now?' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'now' without extra filler words.
'Hold on, hold on, just a second.' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'any minute' and 'any minute' in a few short words.
'Hello. Hello.' The meaning hinges on 'hello' working together with 'hello' in spoken Russian. Dmitry answers right away.
'Dima, where are you?' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'Dima' and 'you' in a few short words.
'I am in that place...' Senya anchors the line on 'I', while 'that' completes the thought.
'At the restaurant.' In Russian, the idea of 'restaurant' flows naturally into 'restaurant' without extra filler words. Senya answers right away.
'Drinking coffee.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'coffee' before landing on 'to drink'.
